mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stabilized at +33% over the last two weeks, indicating lockdown compliance has plateaued. This plateau signals the beginning of behavioral fatigue that will drive retail-recreation mobility upward over the next four weeks as individuals seek relief from confinement.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stabilized at 32.4% and 33.0% in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean, or RESIDENTIAL continues to rise above 35%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has declined from -75.7% to -70.0% over two weeks, indicating essential-goods access is stabilizing. This stabilization reduces the urgency of essential trips and frees behavioral capacity for discretionary retail-recreation visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -75.7% to -70.0% over two weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -72% in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM stabilization.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained near -85% for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES declined only -80.6%, indicating selective workplace reopening without corresponding transit restoration. This mismatch will constrain retail-recreation recovery because commuters lack transport infrastructure, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -84% while WORKPLACES exceeds -82%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -84.9% vs WORKPLACES at -80.6% in t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -75% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite the transit-workplace gap persisting.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized at -76% over two weeks, indicating outdoor activity capacity is exhausted or weather-constrained. This saturation of outdoor alternatives will redirect mobility demand toward indoor retail-recreation venues over the next week, producing a sharp upward shift in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS shows zero week-on-week change for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -77.4% and -76.3% in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to decline below -77%, or RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week of PARKS stabilization.

mechanism_narrative: The convergence of RETAIL_REC (-87.1%), TRANSIT (-84.9%), and WORKPLACES (-80.6%) indicates a coordinated collapse of mobility across all non-residential domains. This synchronized suppression reflects unified lockdown enforcement that will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks unless enforcement visibly relaxes.
candidate_trigger: all three series remain within 10 percentage points of each other
evidence_refs: fact:all three within 6.5 percentage points in t-0w
failure_condition: Any of the three series rises more than 15 percentage points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite synchronized suppression persisting.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has increased from +19.7% to +33.0% over three weeks, indicating sustained indoor confinement. Mid-April seasonal factors (heat, festival preparation) will begin to override lockdown compliance, driving outdoor and retail mobility upward over the next four weeks despite policy constraints.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +32% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 19.7% to 33.0% over three weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to rise above +35%, or RETAIL_REC does not increase by week 3 of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved from -75.7% to -70.0% while RETAIL_REC remains at -87.1%, indicating selective reopening of essential retail only. If this selective policy persists without extending to discretionary retail, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the next two weeks despite essential-goods access improving.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves more than 5 points while RETAIL_REC remains below -85%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -70.0% vs RETAIL_REC at -87.1% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -75% within two weeks, or GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC gap closes below 10 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -80.6% over two weeks while TRANSIT remains at -84.9%, indicating a subset of workers are returning via private transport. This private-transport commuting pattern will extend to retail-recreation trips over the next week, producing a measurable increase in RETAIL_REC despite transit constraints.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves more than 3 points while TRANSIT remains below -84%
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -80.6% while TRANSIT at -84.9% in t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not improve further within one week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of the workplace-transit divergence.
